before: Each w:num counted on its own counter, even when several w:num entries named one w:abstractNum. A list the editor or the automation API started on a reused w:abstractNum wrote a w:num with no level overrides, and a starting number from the automation API was written only as the w:start of a replacement w:lvl.
after: Every w:num over one w:abstractNum counts on one shared counter, and a w:startOverride restarts it once at the first paragraph of that w:num on an overridden level. A list started on a reused w:abstractNum writes one w:lvlOverride with a w:startOverride for each level, and an automation starting number is written as a w:startOverride and as the level w:start.
reason: List numbers are computed locally from the shared package and are not shared state. The new w:num carries ordinary w:lvlOverride and w:startOverride elements, which released participants already store, replicate, and lay out; shared nodes, operations, and package serialization are unchanged.
